desc: Characterize legal moves: they are missing cross-part edges inside a connected bipartite component, or arbitrary edges between two distinct components, with either orientation induced on a merged component.
Analyze component merging: types `(a,b),(c,d)` merge into `(a+c,b+d)` or `(a+d,b+c)` depending on the chosen endpoint colors.
Exhaustively analyze tiny game states to infer a correct closed-form winning criterion, including effects of internal missing edges and merge order.
Prove the game-theoretic winning criterion, including a strategy argument that terminal-edge parity/orientation choices are sufficient.
Verify the criterion on isolated vertices, paths, disconnected edges, equal and unequal bipartition components.
Design and implement an `O(N+M)` BFS/DFS bipartite-coloring solution computing the necessary statistics.
